text.en: Not every individual sport is on a running track. From the 1.15 m service rule in badminton to 11-point rallies in table tennis, gymnastics vaults, tennis sets, and 50 m swimming pools, Chapter 5 covers five major individual sports.

Chapter 5 covers Badminton, Gymnastics, Table Tennis, Tennis, and Swimming.
Badminton is played as singles, doubles, and mixed doubles; during service, the server and receiver stand diagonally, and the shuttle must be below 1.15 m at impact.
Gymnastics includes Artistic, Rhythmic, Trampolining, Tumbling, and Acrobatic gymnastics; men's events include pommel horse and parallel bars, while vault uses a 25 m runway.
Table Tennis is played on a 9 ft × 5 ft × 2.5 ft table with a 6-inch net; a game goes to 11 points (with a 2-point lead at 10-all) using pen-hold or shake-hand grip.
Tennis uses singles and doubles sidelines (the space between them is the doubles alley); matches are best of 3 sets (women) or 3/5 sets (men), with terms like game point and break point.
Swimming is a low-impact full-body sport in a standard 50 m × 25 m pool with 8 lanes; the best swimmer is seeded in lane 4, and relay teammates must wait until the incoming swimmer touches the wall.
Chapter 5 explores five individual sports: Badminton, Gymnastics, Table Tennis, Tennis, and Swimming.
In Badminton, serve diagonally with the shuttle below 1.15 m, and master forehand and backhand grips.
Artistic Gymnastics includes floor, vault (25 m runway), pommel horse, and parallel bars.
Table Tennis games are played to 11 points on a 9 ft by 5 ft table using pen-hold or shake-hand grip.
Tennis courts mark singles sidelines inside doubles sidelines, forming the doubles alley.
A standard Olympic swimming pool is 50 m long with 8 lanes; lane 4 goes to the fastest qualifier.

problem.en: In Table Tennis, the score reaches 10–10. Player A wins the next point to make it 11–10. Has Player A won the game?

why.en: Normally the first to 11 wins, UNLESS both reach 10.

text.en: At 10-all, a player needs a 2-point lead to win (e.g., 12–10), so the game continues.

prompt.en: Compare the scoring or court rules of Badminton, Table Tennis, and Swimming.

requiredIdeas.en: Badminton serves diagonally with shuttle below 1.15 m
Table Tennis is played to 11 points (2-point lead at 10-10)
Standard swimming pool is 50 m long with 8 lanes and no lane changing

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a swimmer can switch lanes mid-race or that 11-10 wins a Table Tennis game

points.en: Badminton features singles/doubles/mixed events and diagonal service below 1.15 m.
Gymnastics has Artistic, Rhythmic, Trampolining, Tumbling, and Acrobatic forms.
Table Tennis (9×5 ft table) is played to 11 points; Tennis uses singles/doubles sidelines and sets.
Swimming pools are 50 m × 25 m with 8 lanes; swimmers must stay in their assigned lane.
